newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo shares fall on Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo shares fall on Q3 results.

text.p: Wells Fargo and Co's shares fell after the bank, which merged with First Interstate Bancorp in April, reported lower than expected earnings for the second quarter in a row.
"This is the second quarter in a row that they've been below expectations," said Ray Soifer, analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.
Wells reported third quarter net of $321 million or $3.23 a share versus $261 million or $5.23 a share and was below First Call's mean estimate of $3.80 a share.

Wells shares fell 3-1/4 to 251-7/8. Back in July, Wells' stock tumbled after it reported disappointing second quarter results in its first earnings release following its $11 billion merger with First Interstate Bancorp.
Higher than expected merger-related costs were cited by analysts for the second quarter's shortfall, and some analysts said expenses dragged on earnings again in the third quarter.
"There's a continued high level of transition expenses due to the First Interstate merger, such as costs for consultants, severance," said David Berry of Keefe, Bruyette Woods.
High credit card loan chargeoffs were also cited.
"Credit card losses are still high at Wells and the bank took a loan loss provision for the first time in over a year," said George Salem, analyst with Gerard Klauer Mattison.

While Wells had told analysts it was planning to reinitiate a loan loss provision this year, several were surprised by the timing of the provision and said they would adjust estimates on views Wells would build on the provision.
"They clearly warned this would come, but they weren't really clear when it would come," Berry said, adding, "I'll probably trim my estimates to reflect the higher provision expense."
Wells' third quarter non-interest expense was $1.3 billion, including a $22 million one-time assessment to replenish the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF).
Analysts said the one-time assessment amounted to $0.14 a share. Excluding the assessment, Wells' earnings translate to about $3.37, which is still below estimates, analysts said.
Berry said he had been forecasting Wells would earn $15.80 a share for full year 1996 versus $20.37 a share in 1995, but he planned to trim his estimate.
First Call's mean estimate is for Wells to report $16.52 a share.
Net charge-offs in the quarter totalled $171 million, or 0.98 percent of average loans. The largest category of net charge-offs was credit card loans, which totalled $95 million.
Wells Fargo's management will hold a conference call with analysts on Wednesday.
"During the third quarter we completed the conversion of our California customer base," Wells chairman Paul Hazen said.
"We owe our employees tremendous thanks for their effort during these past few months and also appreciate the patience our customers have demonstrated throughout this transition period."
